question: Any new rules, consultations or guidance for banks?

decisions.reason: MAS issued an amendment to Notice 643A on bank exposures and credit facilities to related concerns on 4 Sep 2026. It takes effect on 4 Sep 2027.
MAS issued an amendment to Notice 643 on banks' transactions with related parties on 4 Sep 2026. It takes effect on 4 Sep 2027.
MAS issued Amendment No.2 to Notice 656 on 4 Sep 2026. It sets limits on exposures to single counterparty groups for Singapore-incorporated banks and takes effect on 4 Sep 2027.

The Financial Services and Markets (Amendment) Bill 2026 had its first reading on 8 Sep. It would let MAS impose minimum total loss-absorbing capacity (TLAC) requirements on systemically important financial institutions, which include the major banks.
MAS consultation P015-2026, opened 1 Sep, proposes amendments to the Payment Services Act to regulate stablecoins. It closes on 16 Oct.
MAS media release announcing the stablecoin consultation.
News report on the stablecoin consultation, covering the 100% reserve requirement and the ban on paying yield.

MHA, MOF and MAS jointly published a national anti-money laundering strategy, which is policy guidance that affects banks. The article is dated 23 Sep, but its text carries an 'Oct 30' dateline, so the publication date is uncertain.
This is MAS's response on the group capital framework for licensed insurers, so it covers insurers rather than banks.
A bilateral framework with Bank Indonesia for settling trade in local currencies. It is a cooperation arrangement, not a rule or guidance for banks.
A S$220m FinTech funding scheme (FSTI 4.0), which is not regulation.

Prohibition orders against securities representatives. This is enforcement, not rules for banks.

events.title: MAS amended bank Notices 643 (related-party transactions), 643A (exposures to related concerns) and 656 (single counterparty group limits) on 4 Sep 2026, effective 4 Sep 2027.
events.reason: These are binding rule changes aimed directly at banks, which is exactly what the question asks about.

events.title: A bill giving MAS power to impose minimum TLAC requirements on systemically important financial institutions had its first reading in Parliament on 8 Sep.
events.reason: This is a major new resolution-related prudential requirement for systemically important banks.

events.title: MAS opened a consultation (closing 16 Oct) on Payment Services Act amendments to put its stablecoin framework into law, including 100% reserves and a ban on paying yield.
events.reason: This is the period's major consultation, but it targets stablecoin issuers under the Payment Services Act rather than banks. It is worth adding only if space allows.

events.title: Singapore published a national AML strategy produced jointly by MHA, MOF and MAS.
events.reason: High-level national strategy rather than a specific rule for banks. The article's date is also inconsistent.

gold.state_reason: There were several new regulatory items for banks: amended exposure and related-party notices, the TLAC bill and the stablecoin consultation. All are routine rule-making, with no adverse event that needs follow-up.
